evidence_summary: Vladimir Danila was born in Romania and moved to Germany at age 4. His father gave him a programming book, which sparked his interest in coding. By age 10, he was building his own design tool because existing software couldn't handle his illustrations. He launched Vectornator (later Linearity) at 17, making $40,000 in sales almost immediately with no marketing. He won the German ISEF competition and used the prize money to hire a team, partnering with startup advisor Marc Zacherl. Linearity has since raised $20M and counts Apple, Disney, Meta, and Microsoft among its 7 million users.
